questions.stem: A company is evaluating Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and wants to understand its high-level architecture. Which of the following BEST describes how OCI organizes physical infrastructure for high availability within a region?

options.text: Each OCI region contains exactly one data center; high availability comes only from cross-region replication.
An OCI region contains one or more Availability Domains (ADs), and most regions also have multiple Fault Domains within each AD for further isolation against hardware failure.
OCI uses a single global pool of compute with no regional isolation.
OCI does not offer high availability — customers must implement it entirely in their own data centers.

questions.explanation: OCI structures infrastructure into Regions → Availability Domains (ADs) → Fault Domains (FDs). ADs are physically separate data centers within a region; FDs are logical groupings within an AD that share no single point of hardware failure. This three-tier model is the foundation of OCI HA design.

questions.stem: In OCI, which construct is the PRIMARY mechanism for organizing and isolating cloud resources for different teams, projects, or environments — and on which IAM policies are scoped?

options.text: Compartments — a hierarchical container that holds resources and is the scope for IAM policies.
Tenancies — there is one tenancy per resource.
Subnets — IAM policies are attached to subnets.
Tags only — OCI uses tags instead of compartments.

questions.explanation: Compartments are OCI's distinctive resource-organization construct: hierarchical, nestable up to 6 levels, and the scope on which IAM policies are written ("ALLOW group X to manage instances in compartment Y"). Tenancies are top-level (one per OCI subscription). Subnets are networking constructs. Tags add metadata but don't replace compartments.

questions.stem: You need to launch a VM-based web application in OCI. The application must be reachable from the internet on port 443 with a public IP. Which network construct combination is the MINIMUM required setup in OCI?

options.text: A Virtual Cloud Network (VCN) with a public subnet, an Internet Gateway attached to the VCN, a route rule sending 0.0.0.0/0 to the IG, and a Security List or Network Security Group allowing TCP 443 ingress.
Just a tenancy — VMs get internet by default.
A Service Gateway (used to reach Oracle services privately) is sufficient.
A NAT Gateway in a private subnet is the only option for public web traffic.

questions.explanation: The standard OCI public-facing pattern requires a VCN, public subnet, Internet Gateway (IG), a 0.0.0.0/0 → IG route rule, and security list / NSG rules permitting the desired ports. Service Gateway is for private connectivity to Oracle services (Object Storage, etc.). NAT Gateway gives outbound-only internet for private subnets — not for inbound public traffic.

questions.stem: A team needs to launch a Linux VM with consistent CPU performance and predictable cost, using AMD-based x86 hardware. Which OCI Compute shape family fits BEST?

options.text: Standard E-series shapes (e.g. VM.Standard.E4.Flex / E5.Flex) — AMD EPYC, flexible OCPU and memory, predictable pricing.
Ampere A1 shapes — those are Arm-based, not AMD x86.
Bare Metal HPC shapes — those are specialized HPC, not general compute.
GPU shapes — only useful if the workload uses NVIDIA GPUs.

questions.explanation: OCI Standard E-series shapes (E4.Flex, E5.Flex) run on AMD EPYC processors and offer flexible OCPU + memory configuration with predictable pricing — the documented fit for general AMD x86 workloads. Ampere A1 shapes are Arm-based. HPC and GPU shapes target specialized workloads.

questions.stem: A company stores 200 TB of compliance archives in OCI Object Storage. The data is accessed less than once a year, and retrieval can take up to 1 hour. Which Object Storage tier provides the LOWEST cost?

options.text: Archive Storage tier.
Standard tier.
Infrequent Access tier (the alias for Standard since OCI consolidated tiers).
Block Volume — used as cold archival.

questions.explanation: OCI Archive Storage is the lowest-cost Object Storage tier, designed for data accessed less than once a year with retrieval latency of about an hour. Standard is for frequently accessed data. Block Volume is for VM disks, not archival object data.

questions.stem: Which OCI service is responsible for centrally managing customer-controlled encryption keys (including HSM-backed keys) and is integrated with Object Storage, Block Volume, and other OCI services for encryption at rest?

options.text: OCI Vault.
OCI Cloud Guard.
OCI Logging.
OCI Bastion.

questions.explanation: OCI Vault (Key Management) stores and manages encryption keys (including FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM-backed keys) and integrates with Object Storage, Block Volume, Database, and other services for envelope encryption. Cloud Guard is a security-posture / threat-detection service. Logging is for log aggregation. Bastion provides ephemeral SSH access into private subnets.
